description: This package contains author-curated multi-site meteorological records, optical-turbulence measurements, and physics-informed weak labels used in the study.
Four 35-day windows in 2025: Jan 1-Feb 4, Apr 1-May 5, Jul 1-Aug 4, Oct 1-Nov 4; 5-min grid; 40,320 times/station; 403,200 station-times total.
One meteorological record per station-valid_time. lead_min covers 0,5,...,120; issue_time=valid_time-lead. The aligned dataset contains 403,200 station-time records.
Meteorological records were collected, quality-controlled, temporally aligned, and resampled to the unified 5-minute grid used in the study.

Formula 1 is the standard optical conversion reported in the Tatarskii/Gladstone-Dale literature. Formula 2 is the physics-informed surface-layer parameterization used to construct weak labels in this study.
temperature_K, pressure_Pa (converted to hPa), wind_speed_mps, relative_humidity_pct, solar_proxy S, measurement height z, terrain multiplier.
clip[0.35,0.98]{0.96*exp(-lead_min/420)*exp(-0.35*range_penalty)}; range_penalty increases outside broad training-like T/U/RH ranges.
On-site optical-turbulence measurements were quality-controlled; missing, precipitation-screened, saturation-screened, and low-signal records are retained on the time grid with blank values.
Region: join on station. Weather-to-labels: join weather.valid_time_UTC to weak.valid_time_UTC and measured.timestamp_UTC. Final forecast sample key: station + valid_time_UTC + lead_min.

Real global forecast archives generally do not provide native 5-min forecasts. Keep original issue/valid/lead metadata, then interpolate meteorological predictors to 5 min; do not interpolate measured Cn2 across long gaps without a stated method.
